verdict:
The survey is not complete: accurate where it cites, but far from complete. It must not be treated as a PhD-level bibliography until the top-venue sweep and the non-US sweep below are done. Several structural defects must also be fixed before KG ingestion.

**Method.** The session WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200), so ground truth came from five sources:
- Semantic Scholar bulk search, sorted by citation count, with venue filters.
- The arXiv API and abstract pages.
- NVD CVE API 2.0 and Crossref.
- The USENIX Security 2026 technical-sessions page.
- Direct fetches of vendor and government pages.

The corpus is 838 `###` blocks across 6 files (about 820 real entries) with 422 unique arXiv ids.

**Accuracy checks (good overall).**
- arXiv ids: 483 of 484 id/title pairs match arXiv. The one wrong id (Casey et al.) was scraped from reference [67] in the paper's bibliography.
- CVEs: 32 of 34 checked in NVD match. Two are mis-paired: CamoLeak's heading uses CVE-2025-59145, which is actually the color-name npm hijack, and the GrafanaGhost pairing with CVE-2026-27876 is wrong.
- Venues: 41 venue claims marked "per memory" were checked in S2. Nearly all hold. Morris II at CCS 2025 is a retitled version with DOI 10.1145/3719027.3765196.
- URLs: of 60 random URLs, nearly all resolve. 403s come from paywalls or bot walls. ATLAS deep links return 404 to curl because the site is a single-page app.
- ATLAS 2026.09: the counts verify (16 tactics, 208 techniques of which 120 top-level and 88 sub-techniques, 40 mitigations, 73 case studies), and so do the cited case-study ids.
- Extraordinary 2026 claims are real: the OpenAI-agent intrusion at Hugging Face (HF and METR posts), SalesBleed, the Taiwan MODA release, the Anthropic September 2026 report, and the GTIG statistics.
- Enumeration claims verify: CWE 4.20 (2026-04-30, 969 weaknesses), CWE-1448, CAPEC 3.9 still current, ETSI TS 104 158 and EN 304 223, NIST IR 8596 and COSAiS, and GCVE.

**KG-blocking defects.**
- 36 entries map to ATLAS ids deleted in 2026.09. T0019, T0058 and T0104 became T0115.000, .001 and .002.
- 40 papers carry 2 or 3 different ids with conflicting years. This violates the workspace rule that ids are stable.
- 16 group headings at `###` level parse as phantom entries.
- Confidence is miscalibrated: 698 high vs 9 low, including summaries written "from memory".

**Completeness is the failure.** Citation-sorted Semantic Scholar diffs show the gaps venue by venue:
- **Top-4 security venues, LLM papers 2023-26:** 60 of the 80 most-cited are absent, at least 30 of them in scope. Examples: Lukas et al. on PII leakage (S&P 2023), MasterKey (NDSS 2024), JudgeDeceiver (CCS 2024), Malla (USENIX 2024), BAIT, PEFTGuard.
- **Top-4 security venues, ML papers 2016-26:** 57 of 80 are absent, about 30 in scope. Examples: Sharif CCS'16, Hitaj CCS'17, Pierazzi S&P'20, Arp USENIX'22, Hidden Voice Commands, LiDAR CCS'19, Song and Mittal, Ye CCS'22, BadEncoder, Back-to-the-Drawing-Board.
- **SaTML:** 46 of the 50 most-cited papers are absent.
- **NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR attack papers:** 54 of 80 are absent.
- **USENIX Security 2026:** about 70 AI-security papers are listed and the survey has 2.
- **S&P 2026 and CCS 2025:** swept only by keyword, which missed agentic browsers, GPU Rowhammer, TDX, MoE side channels and artifact authentication.

Whole lineages are empty or thin: voice and audio, NLP adversarial examples, GNN and RL, FL poisoning, side-channel and fault attacks before 2019, the classic MIA canon, unlearning attacks, image watermark removal, T2I jailbreaks, AI-generated-code security, and the most-cited LLM-security surveys.

**Imbalance.**
- 85% of dated entries are from 2023-2026.
- 38% of the 391 papers state no venue.
- The incident log is 55% vendor research.
- There is zero government guidance from China (TC260 and CAC, including the September 2026 AI-application and agent-system security guides), Singapore (CSA, IMDA), Japan (AISI), India (CERT-In AIBOM), France (ANSSI), Germany (BSI), Canada or Australia.
- The only non-English source is one Taiwanese press release.
- Israeli government guidance could not be checked (gov.il returned 403). Israeli academic work is only partly represented.
- The incident log is US-centric and misses ByteDance training sabotage, the Grok system-prompt tampering, McHire, and the Slovakia deepfake.
- KG prior art is missing: IBM AI Atlas Nexus, a LinkML risk KG with crosswalks.
- Catalogs are missing: OWASP MCP Top 10 (MCP01-10:2025) and OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10.

**Before the report goes out:**
- Sweep USENIX Security 2025-26, S&P 2025-26, CCS 2024-25, NDSS 2025-26 and SaTML 2023-26 from the official program pages.
- Backfill the classical lineages.
- Add the non-US guidance.
- Fix the suspect entries below.
- Remap ATLAS ids to 2026.09.
- Merge duplicate ids.
